A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BRIDGE research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original SFT and reinforcement-finetuning results on iGSM and PromptBench, alongside behavior ablations, influence analyses, and appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds Qwen-3B results on PromptBench in Table 2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the injected behaviors, and the SFT-to-GRPO procedure remain unchanged. The added DAG-extraction description documents an existing step. Equation (1)'s inserted logarithm corrects the formula to match the negative-log-likelihood objective already stated in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic iGSM and PromptBench tasks with the same in-distribution and out-of-distribution difficulty conditions. The added Qwen-3B results expand model configurations, not datasets or task coverage.

E2.justification: Vanilla, PP-Aug, and RC-Aug remain the comparison methods, including in the added Qwen-3B results. The appendix rejection-sampling comparisons are retained. Dr. GRPO, GPG, and DAPO are discussed theoretically but are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Table 2 extends the reported PromptBench evaluation to Qwen-3B, alongside the existing Qwen-1.5B and Llama-1B configurations. Its stated protocol remains two SFT epochs and 100 RL steps; retained experiments' splits, metrics, preprocessing, and training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The behavior ablations, injection-probability sensitivity, entropy/perplexity analysis, influence diagnostics, and rejection-sampling study are retained. Figures 4 and 5 exchange numbering; Appendix B.7 provides more explanation of an existing analysis rather than new analytical results.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated training runs or seeds, and v2 introduces no new uncertainty estimation or significance testing. Existing distribution plots and training-curve displays retain their reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds Qwen-3B results: BRIDGE achieves 85.8% in-distribution and 70.0% OOD accuracy after RL, versus 44.4% and 31.0% after SFT. These are newly reported configuration-specific results. Existing Table 1 and Table 2 entries and earlier experimental curves remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.2 derives extensions of the existing influence analysis: alpha(1-alpha) for Dr. GRPO, C alpha(1-alpha) for GPG, and a filtered query set for DAPO. Equation (1) gains its missing logarithm. Proposition 3.1, its assumptions, and its original proof are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: rollout accuracy and data co-influence explain RL readiness, and injecting exploratory and exploitative behaviors during SFT improves subsequent RL. Added evidence supports these existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix B.2 newly explains that fixed-format data permit string-matching DAG extraction and warns that extracting from a minimal solution can omit redundant nodes. It also discusses oracle-LLM extraction for unstructured QA. Existing result interpretations and the conclusion's domain limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a DAG-extraction example and an oracle-LLM prompt. Appendix B.7 explicitly describes influence aggregation over the existing 2,000 queries and 16,000 query-output pairs. The abstract replaces the direct repository link with a project-website link; existing hyperparameters and hardware information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting Dr. GRPO, GPG, and DAPO and relates these algorithms to its influence analysis. It removes the explicit PPO example and reference from Section 3.2. The broader related-work discussion and research positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: v2 replaces much RFT terminology with RL, corrects wording, updates the publication header, and adds explanatory appendix subsections. The main section sequence and narrative remain substantially intact; this is localized editing and expansion rather than extensive restructuring.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves into the introduction, Figure 2 is arranged beside Algorithm 1, and the behavior and probability ablation figures exchange numbering and placement. Table 2 gains a Qwen-3B block, and captions and appendix layouts receive limited revisions. Existing graphical results are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through explicit DAG-extraction and influence-estimation instructions, corrects the SFT equation, and supplies concrete derivations for previously asserted extensions to other RL algorithms. The added Qwen-3B PromptBench comparison provides further support across model sizes. These are useful incremental improvements within the existing method, task scope, and conclusions.
